doc.title: Phil Flanigan interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

chapter: Florida life and the jazz scene
title: Florida musicians and the Bread of Life gig
summary: He names local players and tells about the Bread of Life health food store venue.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: What other good musicians are down in your area? I know Ira Sullivan’s down there.
Ira Sullivan, Duffy Jackson, Eddie Higgins, Eric Alison, Pete Minger — now you’ve got me on the spot.
Well that’s okay. Did you ever do that gig at the Bread of Life? You know that place?
Yeah. I did that a couple of times. I did it once with Pete Minger and Eddie Higgins, yeah.
We were down there one time and we went there and saw Ira Sullivan.

Yeah. The owner, his name is Richie Gerber, he is Howard Stern’s cousin, whoop-de-do. He’s an amateur tenor player and always had an interest in music and started having music at this health food restaurant he had. Then he moved to a bigger location which was the big Bread of Life where they just had like a natural food supermarket, and in one little area where you could maybe eat some of the stuff you had just bought, they had a small stage and an upright piano. And it just made for a very strange scene musically, because like Eddie Higgins said, you’re right in the middle of a chorus and you’re just about ready to reach the climax and you hear, “Price check on aisle three, price check.” Like that. And that can sort of kill the momentum of music that might be happening at that particular time. But these are the kinds of things that the politically correct, very psychologically correctly and nicely appropriate sort of mental attitude that you should have these days, would enable you to accept.
You sound like a person who’s not totally happy with the way things are going. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -18-

Well, it has ever been thus I’m sure. But it really separates the people that are trying to learn something day to day, and those who are floating on something, resting on something, their laurels, the status quo or something else, or their little paychecks. And that’s just one of my sociologically astute observations, that’s all.
